notes.buffer.durability: the only tier implemented; `disk` is refused by name
notes.dead_letter:
Where a batch the sink will not take goes. Required, not defaulted: a
stream without one loses a refused batch to a log line, and an operator
who never chose that does not know it is happening.

`files` reads a directory, gs:// and s3://, so this is a folder on a
laptop and a bucket in production with no change to the gateway.

Each record carries _dead_letter_reason, _dead_letter_sink and
_dead_letter_at: whoever finds this file has the events and not the log,
and "why is this here" is their first question.
notes.dead_letter.path:
/var/dead-letter is a VOLUME, not a path inside the image. A dead
letter written to a container's own filesystem dies with the container,
which makes it a slower way of losing the events.
notes.format: json | array | ndjson -- declared, never sniffed
notes.hook: A name in this binary's registry, not a path. Hooks are Go, compiled in.
notes.identity:
What becomes the ingestion_id. All four, because the formula is frozen
over exactly these: leaving one out produces a DIFFERENT id, not a
weaker one. provider and entity are the stream's; source_key and
record_ts name fields of the event.
notes.retry:
How hard the sink is tried before a batch is given up on. Four attempts
over roughly seven seconds: enough to ride out a restart on the other
side, short enough that a sink which is down is known to be down.
notes.sink.attributes:
Fields of the EVENT that travel as message attributes. The topic's
contract belongs to whoever owns the topic, so nothing is invented here.

notes:
A SECOND STREAM, INTO A TABLE. `clicks` above lands in a topic and this
lands in Postgres, side by side on purpose: both are destinations, and
only one of them has columns a SELECT can name. /data shows that
difference -- the table offers Preview and Query, the topic offers no
tabs at all.

And its WRITER is a different kind. `sales.daily` is filled by a
scheduled workflow and this by continuous ingestion, which is what the
freshness column on /data exists to tell apart.
notes.sink.dsn_from:
The NAME of the variable holding the connection string, never the
string: a DSN carries a password and this file is in git.
notes.sink.table:
Schema-qualified, and the table must EXIST. This does not create one,
because a service that creates tables turns a typo here into a second
table nobody is reading. The DDL is in
examples/full-pipeline/warehouse/001-sales.sql.
notes.sink.write:
MERGE AND NOT APPEND, and the gateway refuses to guess: "appending a
redelivery into a table somebody counts and merging into a log that
wanted every arrival are both wrong, and only the table's owner knows
which it is". Orders are counted, so a redelivery must not become a
second row -- which is what `ingestion_id UNIQUE` in the DDL is for.
